phrase.zh: 走过的路，也会成为书页。
phrase.en: The road can become a page.

visual.zh: 巨大的旧皮旅行箱从左侧裁切，空白折纸越过箱沿，斜向展开至右上；红棕书封压在纸下，右下小黄铜指南针与书保持距离。彩色版保留皮革、黄铜、奶油色纸张、暗红布封和灰石的材质差别；黑白版沿用构图。折纸没有路线、地名或文字，道具不是作家的真实行李、手稿或旅程地图。
visual.en: A giant worn leather trunk is cropped at left; blank folded paper crosses its rim and opens diagonally toward upper right. A burgundy book is partly beneath it, separated from a small brass compass. Color distinguishes leather, brass, cream paper, cloth and gray stone; monochrome preserves composition. The sheet has no routes, place names or writing. Props are neither the author’s belongings nor a manuscript or travel map.

background.zh:
海登斯塔姆独享1916年诺贝尔文学奖，获奖理由肯定他作为瑞典文学新时代重要代表的地位。瑞典学院记录他1876至1878年的旅行，以及此后在罗马、巴黎和瑞士的生活；他于1888年以诗集Vallfart och vandringsår进入文坛，作品还包括小说、历史叙事和随笔，1915年出版Nya dikter。配图以旅行箱、折纸与书表现旅行和写作的联系，属于原创解读，不复原任何旅程或作品内容。短句为原创，不是获奖者引语。
1916年文学奖；独享本年度奖项。获奖理由（中文译述）：肯定他作为瑞典文学新时代重要代表的地位
background.en:
Heidenstam received the full 1916 Nobel Prize in Literature, recognized as a leading figure in a new era of Swedish literature. The Swedish Academy records travels in 1876–1878 and subsequent life in Rome, Paris and Switzerland. His 1888 poetry debut was Vallfart och vandringsår; novels, historical narratives and essays followed, with Nya dikter published in 1915. Trunk, folded paper and book are an original interpretation of travel and writing, not a reconstructed journey or text. The phrase is original, not a quotation.
1916 — The Nobel Prize in Literature. Received the full prize. Official motivation: in recognition of his significance as the leading representative of a new era in our literature
